resolutions.researcher_notes: Waha Oil Company's own site (Arabic, archived via Wayback -- live domain 403s the verifier), dated 2020-11-23, reports Phase-1 gas reaching the pipeline's terminal point at Sarir station along the 97 km line ('الخط الواصل إلى محطة السرير بطول 97 كم'), tests underway, full startup expected within days. MEES (2021-01-29, English trade press) independently confirms Sarir plant 'receiving supplies since Phase-1 restart in November 2020'. Libya Observer (2022-07-24) reports the Fargh field 'restarted pumping gas to the Sarir power station' after an interruption -- confirming the line was an established operating asset by then (a restart, not a first start). Three independent origins (operator's own site, an independent MENA energy trade publication, and an independent Libyan news outlet) all describe an actual operating gas flow along this specific Fargh-to-Sarir route across 2020-2022 -- tier high. Note: status has been intermittent (documented interruptions/restarts in 2022), consistent with 'operating' rather than a steady-state claim, which is normal for Libyan infrastructure reporting and not treated as a contradiction.

Both the Waha Oil primary source (natural gas from the Fargh field reaching Sarir station via this line) and MEES (Faregh gas output in mn cfd, gas supply to the Sarir power plant) describe this explicitly as a gas pipeline, not oil/NGL. Two independent origins -- tier high.

Waha Oil's own dated article (2020-11-23) documents Phase-1 gas arriving at the pipeline's Sarir terminus that day, with full commissioning expected within days. MEES (2021-01-29) independently states the Sarir plant has been 'receiving supplies since Phase-1 restart in November 2020'. Both agree on a November 2020 start -- matches sheet StartYear1=2020. Tier high, two independent origins.

Waha Oil Company's own site states verbatim '(بالخط الواصل إلى محطة السرير بطول 97 كم)' -- the line connecting to Sarir station, length 97 km -- an exact match to the sheet's LengthKnown=97.00 km. This is the operator's own primary-source figure, but I could not find a second, independently-authored source stating this specific 97 km figure (English trade press covering the same story -- MEES, Libya Herald, Libya Observer, Petroleum Africa -- report capacity/MW figures but omit route length). Single strong source; tier medium.

Country-level value only (Start/EndCountryOrArea=Libya, no sub-national fields populated in the brief). Both sources place the Fargh field and Sarir station squarely in Libya (Sirte Basin / south-eastern Sahara). Trivial but genuinely corroborated by two independent origins -- tier high.

Operator = شركة الواحة للنفط (Waha Oil Company) is stated directly by Waha's own site (article is published by/about Waha regarding its own Fargh-field-to-Sarir gas line), by MEES ('Faregh gas field ... Operator: Waha Oil Company (Libya)'), and by Libya Observer ('The Fargh field of the Waha Oil Company has restarted pumping gas to the Sarir power station'). Three independent origins -- tier high.

Owner percentages (NOC 59.18%, ConocoPhillips 16.33%, TotalEnergies SE, Hess Corp 8.16%) match verbatim a Total S.A. SEC filing (EX-99.5 to a Form 6-K, an official Total press release dated 10 Dec 2019): 'The NOC (59.18%), Total (16.33%), ConocoPhillips (16.33%) and Hess (8.16%) jointly own the Waha concessions.' url_verifier reports HTTP 403 on this sec.gov URL because SEC blocks the tool's default User-Agent as an undeclared automated client (SEC's documented fair-access policy, not a dead page); manually re-fetched with a declared UA (curl -A 'pipelines-researcher research@globalenergymonitor.org'), got HTTP 200, confirmed '16.33' present verbatim -- this is the same bot-wall false-negative already documented for this exact filing in this batch's P1861 (Farigh-Intesar) shard, reused here since it is the same Waha-concession ownership fact. Independent second source: Hart Energy (2022-11) confirms the same historical structure while reporting Hess's exit ('Hess Completes Libya Asset Sale to TotalEnergies, ConocoPhillips'). Two independent origins (Total/SEC primary filing + independent energy trade press) -- tier high for the STATED sheet values. IMPORTANT CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: this ownership split (Hess Corp 8.16%) is now stale. Multiple independent sources (Hart Energy, S&P Global, MEES 2023-01-27, Oil & Gas Journal, businesswire) confirm Hess sold its full 8.16% Waha stake to TotalEnergies and ConocoPhillips (split evenly, 4.08% each) in a deal that closed 15 Nov 2022; post-transaction, TotalEnergies and ConocoPhillips each hold 20.41%, NOC still 59.18%, and Hess Corp is no longer an owner at all. The sheet's current Owner4='Hess Corp' 8.16% (and Owner3 TotalEnergies with no % shown) reflects the pre-Nov-2022 structure -- refs above support that AS-STATED value but it should be flagged for an update to current (post-2022) ownership.

P3988 (Fargh–Sarir, this row) and P1861 (Farigh-Intesar, per this batch's own P1861 shard) are NOT duplicates of each other: P1861 traces to OPEC ASB2012 Table 4.10 data from 2011 (110 mi / 177 km, 24 in diameter, 7.08 bcm/y capacity -- an older, pre-existing Waha line running Fargh field to the Intisar field/103 complex), while P3988 traces to a 2020 Waha Oil Company announcement of a NEWLY commissioned 97 km line running Fargh field to Sarir GAS/POWER STATION -- different destination, different specs, different vintage, and my primary Waha-2020 source itself distinguishes the two: it describes the Fargh-Sarir line (this row) separately from ongoing supply 'to the Intisar A field ... 70 million cubic meters of gas' (the P1861 corridor), i.e. Fargh field feeds two distinct downstream lines. Good evidence these are two real, separate pieces of infrastructure. P3987 (Intisar–Sarir) is a different question: per GEM's own wiki text, P3987 is described as running from Intisar oil field (Sirte Basin) to Sarir oil field (Cyrenaica), status is explicitly '(presumed operating)' based solely on a 2017 agreement with 'no direct evidence' (GEM's own wording), sourced to a single eanlibya.com URL I could not locate/verify (search engines returned no matching eanlibya.com page under that slug) plus a generic Waha Facebook page and a wahaoil.ly article titled 'إستئناف تغذية خط محطة السرير بشكل اعتيادي' ('resumption of normal supply to the Sarir station LINE') -- that title describes a SUPPLY LINE TO SARIR STATION resuming normal operation, which is the same phrasing/subject as the Fargh–Sarir gas-to-power-station story I independently corroborated for P3988 (Libya Observer 2022-07-24: 'Fargh field ... restarted pumping gas to the Sarir power station'; multiple Arabic sources found this session state plainly 'حقل الفارغ يمثل المصدر الرئيس لتغذية محطة السرير' -- 'the Fargh field is THE MAIN source supplying Sarir station'). I found no independent corroboration anywhere (English or Arabic press, 2017-2026) of a physically distinct 'Intisar oil field to Sarir oil field' gas pipeline separate from the Fargh-to-Sarir line. My working suspicion (not confirmed) is that P3987 may be describing the same underlying Fargh→Sarir gas supply chain/network under an older, less-precise 2017-vintage name (with Intisar possibly an intermediate junction or a source-confusion with the separate Fargh-Intisar line, P1861) rather than a third, independently-built pipeline -- but I could not verify this either way from primary sources, so flagging as UNRESOLVED per protocol rather than asserting duplication. Recommend a human reviewer compare P3987's actual GEM sourcing (the eanlibya.com/wahaoil.ly citations) against this shard's Fargh-Sarir sourcing before any merge/delete decision.
